newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Celesc hopes to issue Level Two ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Celesc hopes to issue Level Two ADRs.

text.p: Santa Catarina state power company Celesc is considering listing its stock on an U.S. stock exchange by issuing Level Two ADRs, said Irineu Theiss, assistant to the company's chief financial officer.

"We are working to launch Level Two ADRs, but no timeframe has been set yet. We are studying the issue," said Theiss before speaking at a conference on Latin American utilities sponsored by Caspian Securities.
Theiss said the company is already doing the groundwork to adapt its accounting methods to U.S. standards.
Celesc already has Level One ADRs, which are traded in the over-the-counter market in the U.S., Theiss said.

Celesc covers 98 percent of electricity demand in southern state of Santa Catarina, serving more than 1.4 million customers. The Santa Catarina state government is the majority shareholder, with 51.1 percent of the firm's voting capital.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom, 5521 5074151))
